clutches_brakes.disk_clutch_uniform_wear.title: Disk clutch torque (uniform wear / worn lining)

variables.name: n
variables.desc: number of friction surfaces (2 for one plate)

variables.name: r_o
variables.desc: outer radius of the friction lining

variables.name: r_i
variables.desc: inner radius of the friction lining

assumptions: Uniform-wear model (worn lining): pressure p = C/r, so the effective radius is the mean radius (r_o + r_i)/2. Peak pressure p_max = F/(2 pi r_i (r_o - r_i)) occurs at the inner edge.

clutches_brakes.disk_clutch_uniform_pres.title: Disk clutch torque (uniform pressure / new lining)

variables.name: n
variables.desc: number of friction surfaces (2 for one plate)

variables.name: r_o
variables.desc: outer radius of the friction lining

variables.name: r_i
variables.desc: inner radius of the friction lining

assumptions: Uniform-pressure model (new, unworn lining): p = F/(pi(r_o^2 - r_i^2)) uniform, effective radius (2/3)(r_o^3 - r_i^3)/(r_o^2 - r_i^2).

clutches_brakes.cone_clutch.title: Cone clutch torque and normal/axial force

variables.name: N
variables.desc: normal force on the conical friction surface

assumptions: Wedge action of the cone raises the normal force to F/sin(alpha); the torque uses the mean radius. A smaller alpha increases torque but risks sticking (alpha should exceed the friction angle to allow disengagement).
method_references: Cone-clutch torque, T = mu F r_m / sin(alpha) (Shigley; recalled)

clutches_brakes.band_brake.title: Band brake tensions, braking torque and peak band pressure

variables.name: mu
variables.desc: friction coefficient between band and drum
variables.label: μ

variables.name: p_max
variables.desc: peak band pressure (at the tight end)

assumptions: Tension relation is the capstan (Euler–Eytelwein) equation, identical to statics.belt_friction. The braking torque is the net band tension times the drum radius. The peak band pressure at the tight end is p = 2 P1/(b D) with drum diameter D = 2 r, i.e. p = P1/(b r).
method_references: Capstan equation; band-brake torque and peak pressure (recalled)

clutches_brakes.drum_brake_short_shoe.title: Short-shoe drum brake: normal force and braking torque

variables.name: F
variables.desc: actuating force applied to the shoe

variables.name: a
variables.desc: perpendicular distance from pivot to the normal-force line of action

variables.name: b
variables.desc: perpendicular distance from pivot to the friction-force line of action

variables.name: c
variables.desc: perpendicular distance from pivot to the actuating-force line of action

procedure.python:
def _drum_short(v):
    """Single internal-expanding short shoe (point-force model).

    sense 'leading' is self-energizing (F = N(a - mu b)/c); 'trailing' adds the friction moment.
    T = mu N r. a, b, c are perpendicular lever arms from the pivot to the lines of action of N, fN
    and F respectively (see module docstring).
    """
    F, mu, r, a, b, c = v['F'], v['mu'], v['r'], v['a'], v['b'], v['c']
    sense = v['sense']
    denom = (a - mu * b) if sense == 'leading' else (a + mu * b)
    if denom <= 0:
        raise MechError('self-locking: a <= mu*b for a leading shoe, so no finite actuating force exists')
    N = F * c / denom
    return {'T': mu * N * r, 'N': N}

assumptions: Short shoe: the lining subtends a small angle so the pressure is uniform and the total normal force acts at the shoe midpoint. Leading shoe: F = N(a - mu b)/c (self-energizing, a > mu b required or the shoe self-locks); trailing shoe: F = N(a + mu b)/c. A two-shoe brake is the sum of one leading and one trailing shoe.
method_references: Short-shoe drum brake moment balance (Juvinall; recalled)

clutches_brakes.drum_brake_long_shoe.title: Long-shoe drum brake: Shigley internal-shoe integrals

variables.name: a
variables.desc: distance from the hinge pin to the drum centre

variables.name: c
variables.desc: lever arm of the actuating force about the pin

variables.name: theta1
variables.desc: shoe toe angle from the hinge pin
variables.label: θ1

variables.name: theta2
variables.desc: shoe heel angle from the hinge pin (θ2 > θ1)
variables.label: θ2

variables.name: M_N
variables.desc: moment of the normal forces about the hinge pin

variables.name: M_f
variables.desc: moment of the friction forces about the hinge pin

procedure.python:
def _drum_long(v):
    """Single internal-expanding long shoe with sinusoidal pressure p = p_a sin(theta)/sin(theta_a).

    The angle of maximum pressure is theta_a = min(theta2, 90 deg): the pressure peaks at the heel when
    the shoe does not wrap past 90 deg, otherwise at 90 deg (so it must also satisfy theta1 <= theta_a).
    Standard internal-shoe integrals (Shigley): moment of normal forces M_N, of friction M_f about the
    hinge pin, braking torque T about the drum centre, and actuating force F = (M_N - M_f)/c for a
    self-energizing (leading) shoe or (M_N + M_f)/c for a trailing shoe. A leading shoe self-locks when
    M_N - M_f <= 0.
    """
    mu, r, b, p_a, a, c = v['mu'], v['r'], v['b'], v['p_a'], v['a'], v['c']
    th1, th2 = v['theta1'], v['theta2']
    sense = v['sense']
    if th2 <= th1:
        raise MechError('theta2 (shoe heel angle) must be greater than theta1 (toe angle)')
    th_a = min(th2, PI / 2)
    if th1 > th_a:
        raise MechError('theta1 (toe angle) must not exceed theta_a (angle of maximum pressure): '
                        'a shoe that wraps past 90 deg must start before 90 deg')
    s = math.sin(th_a)
    if abs(s) < 1e-12:
        raise MechError('theta_a (angle of maximum pressure) must not be 0')
    I1 = 0.5 * (th2 - th1) - 0.25 * (math.sin(2 * th2) - math.sin(2 * th1))
    I2 = r * (math.cos(th1) - math.cos(th2)) - (a / 2.0) * (math.sin(th2) ** 2 - math.sin(th1) ** 2)
    I3 = math.cos(th1) - math.cos(th2)
    M_N = p_a * b * r * a / s * I1
    M_f = mu * p_a * b * r / s * I2
    T = mu * p_a * b * r ** 2 / s * I3
    if sense == 'leading':
        if M_N - M_f <= 0:
            raise MechError('self-locking: for a leading shoe M_N - M_f <= 0, so no finite actuating '
                            'force exists (increase a, reduce mu, or use a trailing shoe)')
        F = (M_N - M_f) / c
    else:
        F = (M_N + M_f) / c
    return {'F': F, 'T': T, 'M_N': M_N, 'M_f': M_f, 'theta_a': th_a}

assumptions: Long shoe with sinusoidal pressure p = p_a sin(theta)/sin(theta_a); the angle of maximum pressure is theta_a = min(theta2, 90°) (at the heel when the shoe does not wrap past 90°, else at 90°). F = (M_N - M_f)/c for a leading (self-energizing) shoe and (M_N + M_f)/c for a trailing shoe; a two-shoe brake pairs one of each. A leading shoe self-locks (M_N - M_f <= 0) and raises an error. Angles measured from the hinge-pin line.
method_references: Internal expanding shoe: Shigley eqs. for M_N, M_f, T (recalled)

clutches_brakes.disk_brake_button.title: Button (circular) pad brake torque

variables.name: F
variables.desc: clamping force on each pad (two pads)

variables.name: r_e
variables.desc: effective radius (pad centre distance from the rotation axis)

assumptions: A small circular button pad carries nearly uniform pressure, so the resultant friction force acts at the pad centre and the effective radius is the centre distance r_e. Two pads, T = 2 mu F r_e.

clutches_brakes.brake_energy.title: Kinetic energy absorbed by a brake (speed change)

variables.name: E
variables.desc: kinetic energy to be absorbed (translational + rotational)

assumptions: Energy removed when speed drops from v1, omega1 to v2, omega2 (set v2 = omega2 = 0 for a stop; keep v2 <= v1 and omega2 <= omega1 so the absorbed energy is non-negative). For a pure flywheel set m = 0 (or v1 = v2); for a pure vehicle set I = 0 (or omega1 = omega2).
method_references: Kinetic energy change, E = 1/2 m (v1^2 - v2^2) + 1/2 I (omega1^2 - omega2^2)

clutches_brakes.brake_stop_time.title: Braking time to a stop (constant torque)

variables.name: t
variables.desc: time to bring the rotor to rest

assumptions: Constant braking torque gives uniform angular deceleration alpha = T/I, so t = omega/alpha. For a translating vehicle the analogous time is t = m v / F_brake.

clutches_brakes.brake_temp_rise.title: Brake temperature rise (adiabatic)

variables.name: cp
variables.desc: specific heat capacity of the brake material

assumptions: Adiabatic single-stop estimate (no cooling, no conduction to other parts): all absorbed energy heats the brake mass. Enter dT in K or delta_degC.

clutches_brakes.flywheel_energy.title: Flywheel energy fluctuation and coefficient of speed fluctuation

variables.name: delta_E
variables.desc: energy fluctuation (largest energy the flywheel stores/returns)
variables.label: ΔE

assumptions: delta_E = 1/2 I (omega_max^2 - omega_min^2) is the exact fluctuation; it also equals I omega_avg^2 C_s. The coefficient C_s is the standard definition.
method_references: Flywheel energy fluctuation; coefficient of speed fluctuation (Shigley; recalled)

clutches_brakes.flywheel_inertia_require.title: Required flywheel inertia for a given speed fluctuation
assumptions: Inverts delta_E = I omega^2 C_s. Combine with flywheel_rim to turn the required inertia into rim dimensions.

clutches_brakes.flywheel_rim.title: Thin-rim flywheel: mass, volume and inertia

variables.name: I
variables.desc: rim moment of inertia about the spin axis

assumptions: Thin rim (t << R) so the whole mass is treated at radius R and I = m R^2; volume is the mean circumference times cross-section. Spokes/hub add a little mass and inertia.

clutches_brakes.flywheel_torque_angle.title: Flywheel energy fluctuation from a turning-moment diagram

variables.name: torque_curve
variables.desc: [[angle (deg), torque (N·m)], ...] over one full cycle, non-decreasing angles (repeat an angle for a vertical step)

variables.name: W_max
variables.desc: maximum cumulative energy above the mean line

variables.name: W_min
variables.desc: minimum cumulative energy above the mean line (typically 0 or negative)

procedure.python:
def _turning_moment(v):
    """Flywheel energy fluctuation from a turning-moment diagram.

    torque_curve: [[angle (deg), torque (N·m)], ...] over one full cycle with strictly increasing
    angles. The mean torque is the trapezoidal average; the cumulative energy W(theta) = integral of
    (T - T_mean) d(theta) gives the fluctuation delta_E = W_max - W_min (largest excess of energy,
    which the flywheel must store and return).
    """
    curve = v['torque_curve']
    if not isinstance(curve, list) or len(curve) < 2:
        raise MechError('torque_curve: [[angle (deg), torque (N·m)], ...] over one full cycle')
    ang = np.array([math.radians(float(row[0])) for row in curve])
    Tq = np.array([float(row[1]) for row in curve])
    if ang[-1] <= ang[0]:
        raise MechError('torque_curve must span a positive angle range (ang_last > ang_first)')
    dth = np.diff(ang)
    if np.any(dth < 0):
        raise MechError('torque_curve angles must be non-decreasing (repeat an angle for a vertical step)')
    Tmean = float(np.trapezoid(Tq, ang) / (ang[-1] - ang[0]))
    W = np.zeros(len(curve))
    for i in range(1, len(curve)):
        W[i] = W[i - 1] + 0.5 * (Tq[i - 1] + Tq[i] - 2 * Tmean) * (ang[i] - ang[i - 1])
    energy_curve = [[float(math.degrees(ang[i])), float(W[i])] for i in range(len(curve))]
    return {'T_mean': Tmean, 'W_max': float(W.max()), 'W_min': float(W.min()),
            'delta_E': float(W.max() - W.min()), 'energy_curve': energy_curve}

assumptions: The torque curve is one complete cycle (a repeating periodic input); the mean torque is the trapezoidal average, and the energy fluctuation is the swing of the cumulative (T - T_mean) integral. delta_E is the energy the flywheel must store and return.
method_references: Turning-moment diagram; energy fluctuation = area between torque curve and mean-torque line
